title: New Hubble image of star cluster Messier 15
caption: The globular cluster Messier 15, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: M 15, Messier 15 · constellation Pegasus · about 35000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Hot blue stars and cooler golden ones swarm together in this Hubble image, crowding ever more densely toward the cluster's bright center. This is Messier 15, a globular cluster some 35,000 light-years away in the constellation Pegasus, the Winged Horse.

At around 12 billion years old, Messier 15 is one of the oldest globular clusters known. It is also one of the densest, with most of its mass packed into its core. A star's color is a guide to its surface temperature, which is why the blue and golden stars here are described as hot and cooler.

The cluster holds more than stars. It was the first star cluster found to contain a planetary nebula, the glowing shell of gas cast off by a dying Sun-like star, and a rare type of black hole has been found at its center. The picture combines Hubble observations across ultraviolet, visible and infrared light.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.48 x 2.66 arcminutes) and distance (35000 light years), the frame spans roughly 25 × 27 light-years. Its light set out about 35,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 and Advanced Camera for Surveys in ultraviolet, visible and infrared light. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet and infrared parts of this image lie beyond what the eye can see.

explore: The picture draws on two Hubble instruments. The Wide Field Camera 3 supplied the ultraviolet and blue exposures, and the Advanced Camera for Surveys supplied the visible and near-infrared ones. Combining them captures both the hot blue stars and the cooler golden ones.
alt: A globular cluster of blue and golden stars that grow more crowded toward a bright center.
